claims.statement: For a finite family of positive block sizes r_i with M=sum_i r_i, coefficient polynomials f_i(t)>=binom(r_i,t), the joint hypergeometric count-vector identity, Jensen bound, logarithmic lower bound, and finite Taylor lower bound give H[k]>=binom(M,k)E_d(y_k) for 0<=k<=M; include the empty family at M=k=0.
claims.scope: Universal abstract finite-block coefficient inequality on 0<=k<=M, with positive block sizes and nonnegative coefficient surplus; empty family is included separately. No probability formula is used outside its in-range domain. No graph rank, selector, payment or arbitrary-tree conclusion.
claims.reason: Count-vector expansion proves the exact expectation; Jensen applies to the dependent joint law. The derivative of log(w)-2(w-1)/(w+1) is nonnegative for w>=1 with positive denominator, and y>=0 makes every omitted Taylor term nonnegative. Producer boundaries and separate exact coefficient checks replayed, but this informal argument has no Lean award.

claims.statement: For finite disjoint positive-size blocks B_r=(1+z)^r+z, the exact singleton-occupancy expectation and Jensen lower bound hold for 0<=k<=M; the zero-extended coefficient floor can be convolved with the nonnegative path-star marked factor G F_r to lower-bound T_i[j].
claims.scope: The special occupancy/Jensen cofactor claim only, including size-one blocks, empty family, in-range normalized formulas, zero-extended coefficient floor, and nonnegative path-star convolution. It asserts no first-descent, rank transfer, strict selector, mass, payment or arbitrary-tree result.
claims.reason: The singleton factor has coefficient ratio 1+1/r only at count one. The joint occupancy expectation and Jensen argument are valid without independence. At k=0 probabilities vanish; at k=M size-one and larger blocks have the stated distinct boundary behavior.

claims.statement: A graph independence polynomial with independence number r coefficientwise dominates (1+z)^r; if it has a vertex outside a fixed maximum independent set, it dominates (1+z)^r+z. A finite-block bound applies to a product of such factors when its disjoint-component factorization is proved.
claims.scope: Coefficient domination and product coefficient bounds only. Parent/deletion factorization, changed marked-component rank, exact parent sequence, actual least strict zero-extended descent, all eligibility guards at the same p, strict current-p selectors, and original tip multiplicities must be established separately before any payment use.
claims.reason: Maximum-independent-set subsets give the binomial floor and an outside vertex supplies one additional singleton. These facts provide no automatic parent-rank, marked-deletion or selector transfer.

claims.statement: For every nonempty ordinary arity-2,3,4 path-star, each original leaf deletion A_v satisfies A_v[k+1]C[k-1]<=A_v[k]C[k] for natural k with 1<=k and 2k<=N+2, using integer zero-extended coefficients.
claims.scope: Guarded coefficient comparison only, no eligibility premise. Any selector application must separately preserve actual least strict parent descent x (including terminal differences; flats are not descent), x+2<=p, 3p<2(N+2)+1, 2p<=N+2, strict Delta_p A_v<0, and original distinct tags/multiplicities.
claims.reason: No guarded counterexample or proof was found. Small exact monomial-basis checks pass but are bounded evidence. The known k=77 obstruction has 2k=154>N+2=82 and is outside the guard.

claims.statement: For every nonempty ordinary arity-2,3,4 path-star, W=sum_i r_i A_i with original private-tip multiplicities satisfies W[k+1]C[k-1]<=W[k]C[k] for natural k with 1<=k and 2k<=N+2, using integer zero-extended coefficients.
claims.scope: Guarded weighted-deck coefficient comparison only, no eligibility premise. Any payment application must retain actual least strict descent, all guards x+2<=p, 3p<2(N+2)+1 and 2p<=N+2, strict current-p selectors, and original r_i multiplicities. A strict W descent only implies at least one selected branch.
claims.reason: No guarded counterexample or universal proof was obtained. Exact small-profile checks pass only as bounded diagnostics; the unguarded k=77 witness violates the target guard.

limitations: The general finite-block Jensen proof is informal and nonformal; its exact checks do not prove universal shifted comparisons.
Guarded shifted comparisons were sampled only on six small profiles and selected ranks; no broad census or universal argument was produced.
Graph coefficient domination does not transfer actual parent rank, marked-deletion identity, strict selectors or payment.
No Lean build, source edit, controller operation, agent delegation or external messaging was performed.
